system.summary: Two keys, each a homophonic letter alphabet of signs plus three-letter lower-case code groups for common words and names.
system.sibling_key: Key B also in R9844 (9/30 ff. 34-36, Soria to Gattinara, Dec 1523) with the court's decipherment.
system.notes: Key A (June-July 1523): ~25 signs, a few homophones, word division kept, code words (leh=en). Key B (from late July 1523): homophonic letters + many three-letter codes, crib from R9844.

solution.what: Fetched all 35 images of R9488-R9498 and the metadata via the DECODE API.
CSP Spain vol. 2 (BHO): only f. 577 calendared, from the clear parts.
Searched DECODE for decrypted Soria records; found R9844 (9/30) with cipher and court decipherment in key B.
Checked the BRAH 9/15 key book (R9815-R9832) for either key; no alphabet matches.
Checked a decrypted 9/28 sibling of another envoy (Alonso Sanchez, R9768) for a shared key; different cipher.
Aligned the first R9844 cipher lines with the clear: code groups sub, yed, xab, xin, xud, si, tef, zeb and a dozen letter values.
Read R9497 (13 Aug 1523) key-B cipher lines 1-7 with the R9844 key: Andrea Doria and the Prince of Salerno discontented with the King of France; approach via Jeronimo Doria.
Subagent read R9494 (26 Jul 1523) key-B blocks: courier, 28,000 escudos for Swiss in Constance, 12,000 to the treasurer; collated with R9495.
Subagent first pass on R9491 (20 Jul, to Gattinara) key-B block: Siena under the Emperor's hand; much of the key-B letter alphabet in this letter still unassigned.
Transcribed R9492 f. 444r-445v key-A block (~1060 signs, 31 lines) with an ASCII glyph scheme.
Sign counts showed ~25 signs, word division kept, lone 'f' 10x (=y), c followed by T 43x (a c+T ligature).

Simulated-annealing substitution solver with a 4-gram model of Danvila's 1520-21 Castilian documents; 'f'=y fixed; found the key-A alphabet (liga general, cinco mil infantes, exercito) from random starts; c+T merged as d.
Hand refinement: alpha=o, q=o (lone q = que), 9/p=a, z=e, e/n=s, c=n, 2=l, code leh=en.
June letter transcribed and collated across its three copies (R9488 full, R9489 full, R9490 spot); copy-to-copy variants confirmed the key-A homophones and fixed code words cip, mos, lim.
June letter read end to end with key A; cap=que, lod=de, luc=duque, lih=Milan from context.
R9492 key-A block re-read at high zoom and collated with the duplicate R9493; d=m, long-stem hook=f corrected; reads continuously.
Key-B passages of R9491 (Siena), R9492 f.448, R9494 and R9497 read in substance; Beaurain identified.

Lasry review (email 25 Sept 2026): key B used plaintext from outside the target (R9844 decipherment), so the target is not 100% ciphertext-only. Method changed from 'key recovered from ciphertext-only' to 'key recovered based on plaintext from external sources'; key A remains a ciphertext-only break.

outcome.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
outcome.method_basis: Key B was rebuilt from an external plaintext, the court's decipherment of Soria's 30 Dec 1523 letter R9844 (Salazar 9/30), and gives the key-B passages in substance; key A, which carries the June and July letters (R9488-R9492), was broken from the ciphertext alone by simulated annealing with a Castilian 4-gram model plus hand fixes. Classed by the key-B route, as Lasry advised (25 Sept 2026): the target as a whole is not ciphertext-only.
outcome.notes: June and July key-A letters read nearly throughout; key-B passages in substance. Open: key-A codes rip, pur, qed, mul; about a dozen key-B groups. fraction_read is an estimate from the NOTES (share of cipher tokens given a value), not measured.

gaps.item: key-A code words rip, pur, qed, mul, dus, cop and the opener TZ
gaps.detail: 1-3 occurrences each, rip/pur/qed guessed from context only

gaps.item: key-B groups yac, fob, taf, tu, pel, pug, zib, sib, xif, sab, 7 pes, per (and guessed paf, tin, sud, xa)
gaps.detail: not attested in the R9844 crib

gaps.item: R9491 lines 1-7 and the personal names in R9494 (grade M)

outcome.fraction_read_source: read_r94*.md: readings are line tables mixing clear and cipher with prose glosses, not token-aligned, so a token share cannot be counted; 0.85 is the NOTES estimate
